collection.description: A child who was present at several accidents fears they bring bad luck.

premise.name: The premise
premise.text: A child has been present at several accidents and fears they cause bad luck.

a.name: Answer A
a.text: An adult teaches the child that fear need not dictate their future.

b.name: Answer B
b.text: A parent explains that accidents happen without a person causing them.

c.name: Answer C
c.text: An elder reassures the child that they deserve love and belonging.

d.name: Answer D
d.text: A researcher examines the incidents and finds no causal link to the child.

r1.name: Resolution 1
r1.text: The villager discovers a plausible ordinary cause but may still value the experience for personal reasons.

text_only.reason: a memory of what happened, not a skill's experience: nothing is gained

r2.name: Resolution 2
r2.text: A second witness or unexpected detail complicates the simplest explanation.

r3.name: Resolution 3
r3.text: Another villager interprets the same evidence differently. Their exchange can deepen respect, cause a mild argument, or inspire a shared project.
